question: Which tribe was Hyram from?
summary: 1 Kings 7:13-14 says Hiram, Solomon's master craftsman, was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali. 2 Chronicles 2:13-14 says his mother was from the tribe of Dan. The two texts identify the same craftsman's maternal lineage as belonging to two different Israelite tribes.

reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read the two tribes as one woman's overlapping ties — a Danite by birth widowed into Naphtali, so both labels fit.

discrepancy.connective: Raymond B. Dillard argues the difference is no accident of a woman's two marriages but the Chronicler's deliberate redaction: he changed Hiram's tribe from Naphtali to Dan to make the craftsman a second Oholiab, the Danite artisan of the Tabernacle.

skeptic.name: Raymond B. Dillard

excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB explicitly names the Naphtali/Dan discrepancy and offers the dual-marriage harmonization that resolves it — the single strongest, most concise reconcile on the row; parity-capped to one because the discrepancy pole carries one named-skeptic connective.
excerpts.source_note_text:
He was a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali--In Ch2 2:14 his mother is said to have been of the daughters of Dan. The apparent discrepancy may be reconciled thus: Hiram's mother, though belonging to the tribe of Dan, had been married to a Naphtalite, so that when married afterwards to a Tyrian, she might be described as a widow of the tribe of Naphtali. Or, if she was a native of the city Dan (Laish), she might be said to be of the daughters of Dan, as born in that place; and of the tribe of Naphtali, as really belonging to it.
a worker in brass--This refers particularly to the works described in this chapter. But in Ch2 2:13 his artistic skill is represented as extending to a great variety of departments. In fact, he was appointed, from his great natural talents and acquired skill, to superintend the execution of all the works of art in the temple.
